text: The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria and pyuria, suggesting an active infection or inflammation despite negative nitrites. To differentiate between a simple urinary tract infection, pyelonephritis, or a stone with secondary infection, I need to visualize the anatomy. REQUEST TEST: CT_Kidney_Ureter_Bladder

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal CT scan rules out kidney stones and structural abnormalities, which is significant given your flank pain and history of recurrent UTIs. Do you experience pain that radiates to your groin or have you noticed any weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recurrent UTIs, hematuria, and pyuria with a normal CT scan, I need to rule out a bladder source for your symptoms. Have you experienced any urgency, frequency, or suprapubic pain, and do you have any known allergies or family history of kidney disease? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal cystoscopy rules out bladder pathology, so we must look higher up the urinary tract. Have you experienced any fever or chills, and do you have a history of kidney stones or gout? REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and cystoscopy, but persistent pyuria and hematuria, I need to rule out a chronic low-grade infection. I will send the urine for specific culture and sensitivity testing. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative urine culture despite pyuria is a critical finding known as sterile pyuria, which strongly suggests an atypical infection or non-infectious inflammation. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and flank pain, I must rule out renal tuberculosis. Do you have any history of exposure to tuberculosis or unexplained weight loss and night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Acid_Fast_Bacilli_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: With sterile pyuria, negative cultures, and negative TB testing alongside recurrent UTIs and flank pain, the clinical picture strongly points towards an inflammatory condition of the kidney parenchyma. I am diagnosing this as Interstitial Cystitis or likely Chronic Pyelonephritis given the recurrent history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Pyelonephritis
